title: Reject invalid Minimal API input before the handler runs
goal: Use registered synchronous DataAnnotations validation for Minimal API request models on .NET 10 or later; replace a custom .NET 9 endpoint filter and verify invalid requests cause no handler work.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: Use the matching ASP.NET Core server runtime. Recorded .NET 11 execution uses RC2, not GA.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: An SDK supporting this target is required; exact authoring pin is 10.0.402.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Declared example language mode, separate from runtime requirements.

packageAssets: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App net10.0 shared validation/generator assets; no extra package.
providers: Kestrel loopback HTTP; no external service or account.
platforms: ASP.NET Core server platforms; executed Windows x64 only. No AOT/WASI claim.
renderingModes: Server JSON HTTP endpoints; no component rendering mode.
prerequisites: Keep each complete project in a separate directory using the shown build/package boundary, SDK pin and source files. Restore the declared assets before running. Guidance retrieval itself is offline.
constraints: Synchronous DataAnnotations validation of a public same-assembly request model before the Minimal API handler. Binding/JSON parsing and business validation are separate. AddValidation must execute in the assembly containing the endpoint/model for generated metadata; moving models/endpoints requires registration in their assembly too. No asynchronous IAsyncValidatableObject implementation, external business check, auth, persistence or strict unmapped-JSON-member contract.
stabilityLimitations: AddValidation/filter are stable; low-level .NET 10 experimental APIs are not used. .NET 11 evidence is RC2; GA reconciliation remains pending.

selectionNotes: Synchronous same-assembly model/endpoint discovery; binding and business rules are separate. Async validation is a later edition.

sources.title: Built-in synchronous Minimal API validation and assembly discovery

evidence.scope: Actual Windows x64 .NET 9 servicing runtime compilation/execution: four real HTTP requests prove invalid fields and malformed JSON return 400 before handler execution, a valid request executes once and a separate business conflict returns 409 from the handler. No mocks, cross-compilation or asynchronous validation. Generated model discovery is exercised by actual invalid-field rejection, not inferred from source.
